title: How to make a small SUV slightly smaller: The 2028 Volvo XC40
gist: Volvo is giving the XC40 crossover a rare second mid-cycle refresh for model year 2028, using design tweaks to visually shrink the small SUV, adding Google Gemini AI to its infotainment, and layering on more radar/camera safety hardware, while withholding the electric EX40 version from the US market.

insights.claim: Volvo is giving the XC40 a second mid-cycle facelift for model year 2028, after an initial launch in 2017 and a first refresh in 2023, an unusually long refresh cadence extension for a single model generation.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Signals Volvo is prioritizing sweating a proven, popular platform over launching an all-new replacement, likely to control R&D spend while keeping a top seller current.
insights.quote: Rather than launch an all-new version, it has decided to give the popular crossover another update for MY28 with the aim of keeping things fresh.
insights.locator: Most cars get a midlife facelift

insights.claim: Akhil Krishnan, interim lead for Volvo's 30 and 40 Series, says the refreshed design, technology, and safety features make this 'the best version of the XC40 yet' and expects it to remain one of Volvo's best-selling models for years to come.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Management is explicitly betting continued XC40 sales strength on incremental refreshes rather than a redesign, indicating confidence in the existing platform's commercial durability.
insights.quote: By enhancing the XC40’s design, technology, and safety features, we’ve created the best version of the XC40 yet
insights.locator: Akhil Krishnan quote, interim lead for 30 and 40 Series

insights.claim: Volvo's designers deliberately shaved corners and volume off the XC40 to make the small SUV appear visually smaller from a pedestrian's perspective, running counter to the industry trend of ever-larger SUVs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A design choice to shrink perceived footprint for pedestrian safety/social optics could differentiate Volvo on safety branding versus competitors chasing size for perceived value.
insights.quote: From a pedestrian’s perspective, the effect is to make the car seem smaller, with its edges slightly farther away.

insights.claim: The refreshed XC40 adds a new 11.2-inch touchscreen running Android Automotive OS with Google Automotive Services, now integrated with Google's Gemini AI as the voice assistant.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows Google extending Gemini's footprint into automotive infotainment through existing Android Automotive OEM partners, a distribution channel investors should track for Gemini's reach beyond phones.

insights.claim: The author's limited hands-on testing found the new Gemini-based voice assistant more capable than the system it replaces in the XC40.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Early qualitative evidence that Gemini integration is a functional upgrade, not just a branding change, relevant to how Google monetizes Gemini via automotive OEM deals.
insights.quote: The addition of more AI will raise many eyebrows, but based on my limited testing, it is more capable as a voice assistant than the one it replaces.

insights.claim: The 2028 XC40 gains a new suite of front, rear, and corner radars, a new forward-looking camera, additional ultrasonic sensors, and revised software with an upgraded 3D view for 360-degree fused parking cameras.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Incremental sensor stacking on a mainstream compact SUV illustrates how ADAS hardware content per vehicle keeps rising even on non-flagship, non-luxury trims, a tailwind for radar/camera/sensor suppliers.
insights.locator: Volvo being Volvo, it couldn’t resist

themes.theme: US market exclusion for EV variant

insights.claim: The revised electric EX40, which shares the same styling changes as the refreshed XC40, will not be sold in the United States.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Another data point on automakers pulling back EV model availability from the US market, relevant to tracking EV demand softness and tariff/incentive dynamics in the US versus other regions.
insights.quote: There’s also a revised electric EX40 that benefits from the same styling changes, but the US won’t get that one.

insights.claim: The refreshed 2028 Volvo XC40 enters production later in 2026 and is expected to go on sale in 2027.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete timeline for when this refreshed model's sales contribution would show up in Volvo's results.
insights.locator: The revised 2028 Volvo XC40 goes into production
